title: AI-Assisted RNA-Seq Analysis with R
text:
Start with a question about differential gene expression. Learn a complete workflow using fictional counts, repeat it using real airway data, and then adapt it to your study. Check inputs, verify outputs, and explain what the analysis can establish.






One workflow for every dataset




Define the question and contrast.
Preview the results you will produce.
Meet the inputs and understand their structure.
Check the inputs and design.
Run the analysis using a documented command.
Verify and explain tables, figures, and limitations.
Write the report with evidence and limitations.






Dataset
Input
Main learning goal




Synthetic practice
Fictional integer gene counts, six paired donors in two conditions
Learn checks, DESeq2 outputs, and independent sample verification


Airway case study
Gene counts from four cell lines measured untreated and treated
Include cell line in the design and interpret a real experiment


Your own study
Your count matrix and study metadata
Check design and adapt the workflow responsibly



This guide starts with gene-level count tables. It does not process FASTQ reads, align sequences, or quantify transcripts. Differential expression describes an association with the specified contrast under the chosen design; it does not alone establish causation outside the experiment or clinical benefit.
Next: Set up the workspace
crumbs: 1  AI-Assisted RNA-Seq Analysis with R

title: Required setup
text:
1. Gather the software
This page takes you from the downloaded project to your first successful RNA-seq input check. R runs the analysis; Quarto renders the lessons and reports.
Install R, Quarto and an editor such as VS Code or RStudio. Reopen the terminal after installing R so it can find Rscript.
You can run the R analysis before installing Quarto. Quarto is needed when you want to preview or render the QMD guide and reports.

title: Required setup
text:
2. Download and open the project

Open the AI-Assisted RNA-Seq Analysis repository.
Select the green Code button, then Download ZIP.
Extract the downloaded ZIP. The folder is usually named ai-assisted-rnaseq-analysis-main. Do not work inside the compressed ZIP.
In VS Code, choose File → Open Folder and select the extracted folder.
Check the file list: _quarto.yml, data/, scripts/ and examples/ should appear directly inside it.
Choose Terminal → New Terminal.

This is the main project folder. Run all guide commands here. You can keep the downloaded folder name; no renaming is required. If extraction created an extra outer folder, open the inner folder containing _quarto.yml.
Check the folder and R installation:

macOS or Linux terminal
pwd
ls
Rscript --version


Windows PowerShell
Get-Location
Get-ChildItem
Rscript --version
If the expected files are missing, reopen the correct folder and a new terminal before continuing. If Rscript is missing, install R or reopen the terminal after installation.

title: Required setup
text:
3. Create the R package environment
renv keeps packages in a project-specific library. The commands set a CRAN mirror explicitly so R does not stop at “Please select a CRAN mirror for use in this session”. Open an R console with the main project folder as its working directory. Confirm with getwd() before proceeding. Follow only the route that applies to your files.

If the project includes renv.lock
Install renv if needed and restore its recorded package versions:
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
install.packages("renv")
renv::restore()
stopifnot(requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE))
renv::status()
Wait for restoration to finish and read any errors. This route applies once a tested lockfile and the renv activation files have been added to the project.


For this starter ZIP without a lockfile
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
install.packages("renv")
renv::init(bare = TRUE)
renv::install(c("BiocManager", "ggplot2"))
BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "airway", "SummarizedExperiment"), ask = FALSE)
stopifnot(
  requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE),
  requireNamespace("airway", quietly = TRUE),
  requireNamespace("SummarizedExperiment", quietly = TRUE),
  requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
)
renv::status()
init() creates .Rprofile, renv/activate.R and a local project library. If R restarts, reopen the project and continue in its environment. The stopifnot() check must finish without an error; it confirms the four packages are available in this R session. If DESeq2 is missing, run BiocManager::install("DESeq2", ask = FALSE) in the activated project and inspect any installation error before trying again.
If renv::status() lists airway, DESeq2 or SummarizedExperiment as missing: these are Bioconductor packages. Install them with BiocManager::install(c("airway", "DESeq2", "SummarizedExperiment"), ask = FALSE) or use their explicit renv sources:
renv::install(c("bioc::airway", "bioc::DESeq2", "bioc::SummarizedExperiment"))
stopifnot(requireNamespace("airway", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("SummarizedExperiment", quietly = TRUE))
renv::status()
Do not use renv::install("airway") without the bioc:: prefix: it may search the CRAN repository and report that airway is unavailable. If an explicit Bioconductor install also fails, keep the download or installation error above the final message for diagnosis. Do not snapshot a project while required packages remain missing.
Once the analysis has run successfully, record the installed versions in the project lockfile:
renv::snapshot()
renv::status()
q(save = "no")
When sharing the project, include renv.lock, .Rprofile and renv/activate.R; leave out the machine-specific renv/library/. The starter ZIP contains no lockfile because a portable project renv lockfile has not been generated. The bundled previews have their own tested run logs and session information. renv should activate when R starts in the initialized project. renv::status() checks its state.
Run these expressions at an R prompt, not in Bash or PowerShell. To exit an R console, use q(save = "no") before entering Rscript commands in the terminal.

title: Required setup
text:
4. Check the synthetic inputs
From the main project folder:
Rscript scripts/R/run_workflow.R data/synthetic results/synthetic --check-only
Expect 12 samples, 2,000 genes and design ~donor + group. This checks file structure, matching sample IDs, nonnegative integer counts and basic replication. It does not run DESeq2 or refresh old results.
The full run needs DESeq2 and ggplot2, while --check-only stops before loading them. To confirm that the terminal uses the same project library as the R console, run:
Rscript -e 'cat("DESeq2 available:", requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE), "\n"); print(.libPaths())'
It should print DESeq2 available: TRUE. If the console check passes but this says FALSE, confirm you are in the main project folder and that its .Rprofile and renv/activate.R exist. Restart the terminal there and repeat the check. On Windows PowerShell, use the same single-quoted command.






Setup checkpoint



Continue when the packages load in the project environment and the input check passes. If installation fails, resolve the complete error before running the analysis.

text:
6. Preview or render
quarto preview
Press Ctrl+C to stop preview. quarto render builds the complete guide. Rendering displays instructions; it does not run the analysis. To render a completed report after running the workflow, use quarto render reports/synthetic-report.qmd --to html.

title: Required setup
text:
Return for another session
Open the same project folder. Its .Rprofile activates renv when R starts. Check renv::status() in R; if the lockfile and local library disagree, run renv::restore() before proceeding. Then use the --check-only command above to confirm the inputs.
Next: Start synthetic practice

title: Synthetic practice: learn the workflow
text:
Start after Required setup. The 2,000 fictional genes and groups A and B were constructed for teaching; do not give them biological names or treat their statistical signals as findings about an organism.






Our question



Which fictional genes have different model-estimated counts in group B compared with group A, and how can we verify and explain the outputs?


Each of six fictional donors has one A sample and one B sample. The model accounts for donor before estimating the B-versus-A effect, preparing you for airway’s paired cell-line design.
By the end you will match 12 sample IDs across two files, check the design and counts, run the supplied R workflow, verify A01 independently, explain the sign of a fold change, and write a short report.



Lesson
Task




Preview
Explore six prepared figures and their supporting tables


Meet
Inspect samples, gene counts and group labels


Check
Validate format, IDs, replicates and contrast


Run
Reproduce all six figures, tables and run record


Verify
Independently calculate A01’s count summary


Write
Report evidence, interpretation and limits



Run shell commands in the terminal from the main project folder. Run R expressions in the R console or in a saved .R script. Quarto rendering displays the guide; it does not execute the analysis.
Before continuing: explain why an A/B result in invented data cannot be presented as a biological discovery.
Next: Preview the results
crumbs: 3  Synthetic practice: learn the workflow

title: See the result
text:
Library sizes
Start by exploring the prepared results from the fictional paired experiment. You can view these figures before running any analysis. Later, you will check the inputs, reproduce the same figures and verify selected numbers.
The preview figures and supporting tables are bundled in results/synthetic/. They were generated by scripts/R/run_workflow.R, which is also used for your practice run. Quarto displays the saved images; rendering does not fit DESeq2.
Comparison direction: positive log2 fold changes mean higher expression in B relative to A. Check this against run-log.txt before interpreting a gene.
Each bar sums the supplied raw gene counts for one sample. Unequal totals motivate normalization; they do not describe overall FASTQ or alignment quality.

title: See the result
text: Library sizes for the fictional paired experiment.

title: See the result
text:
PCA



PCA for the fictional paired experiment.


Each point is a sample; colour shows condition and shape shows donor or cell line. Grey lines connect paired samples. Axis labels give the variation explained. PCA uses up to 500 most variable genes after variance stabilization. Donor variation remains visible: including donor in the fitted model does not remove it from these transformed counts.

title: See the result
text:
Sample-distance heatmap



Sample-distance heatmap for the fictional paired experiment.


Each tile is a Euclidean distance between two samples, using all retained variance-stabilized genes. Darker tiles indicate larger distances. Rows and columns follow hierarchical clustering; diagonal distances are zero. The two annotation strips identify donor and condition. In this bundled simulation, donor pairs sit next to each other in the clustered order: donor variation remains important even with a condition effect. Compare both treatment and donor labels.

title: See the result
text:
MA plot



MA plot for the fictional paired experiment.


Each point is a retained gene with a finite fold-change estimate. The horizontal axis is the mean normalized count on a log scale; the vertical axis is the unshrunken log2 fold change. Colours distinguish adjusted p-values below 0.05, other available values and unavailable values. Low-count estimates may be unstable.

title: See the result
text:
Volcano plot



Volcano plot for the fictional paired experiment.


Each point has a finite fold-change estimate and an available adjusted p-value. The vertical axis is -log10(adjusted p-value), so higher points have smaller adjusted p-values. The dashed horizontal line marks 0.05. Missing adjusted p-values are omitted; numerical zeros are floored for display. The plot uses unshrunken effects and does not impose an effect-size cutoff.

title: See the result
text:
Selected-gene expression



Selected-gene expression for the fictional paired experiment.


Each point is a DESeq2 normalized count; lines connect the same donor or cell line across conditions. The three panels show the gene with the lowest available adjusted p-value, a prespecified gene with no simulated condition effect, and a prespecified gene with variable donor response. The latter two were chosen before fitting, using plot-examples.tsv. “No simulated effect” describes the generating parameter; its observed counts and fitted effect can still differ between conditions. Each panel has its own vertical scale. The first gene is selected after analysis and is illustrative. Normalized counts adjust for size factors; they do not remove donor effects or independently validate the model.

title: See the result
section: Numbers to locate in the bundled results
text:
Numbers to locate in the bundled results
This version has 2,000 fictional genes and 12 samples from six paired donors. A01 has 629,417 supplied counts and 1935 detected genes. After filtering, 1,839 genes are retained in the DE result. Compare input gene count, detected genes for one sample, retained genes and genes with available adjusted p-values: they are different quantities.
PC1 explains 19.4% and PC2 16.7% of variation among the 500 genes used for PCA. The retained genes used for the distance heatmap are a larger set, so the two displays need not emphasize identical patterns.
The post-analysis selected gene is Gene_1515, with estimated log2 fold change 2.391 and adjusted p-value 1.6e-31, for B relative to A while accounting for donor. Its large, consistent change is only one example. Compare it with Gene_0002 (no simulated condition effect) and Gene_0003 (variable donor response), whose panels use separate vertical scales.
These values identify the bundled run; after changing inputs or software, report your own checked outputs. All labels and generating effects are fictional.

title: See the result
text:
Check your understanding

Which samples are paired, and where can you see those pairs?
Does a PCA separation identify statistically significant genes?
Which direction does a positive log2 fold change represent?
Why might a large fold change have weak statistical evidence?
Why is a selected-gene plot not an independent confirmation of its adjusted p-value?

All gene labels and effects here are fictional. Do not assign real biological mechanisms to them.
Next: Meet the data

title: Meet the data
text:
Why this simulation has more variation
Two TSV files connect on sample IDs:
Samples are columns in counts and rows in metadata. Exact spelling and case matter. A zero is a count of zero in this file; a missing value is unknown and needs investigation.
Inspect the files in an R console opened in the main project folder:
Expect 2,000 genes and six fictional donors, each measured once in A and once in B. Look up Gene_0001 for A01 and B01, but do not infer its model estimate from just those two raw values. Gene-level inference combines replicates, normalization, dispersion and the study design.
Most genes have no simulated condition effect. Changed genes have different effect sizes and directions. Baseline expression, donor effects and count variability differ across genes. Twenty genes have a zero generating mean; other low-count genes may also fail the analysis filter. A sample’s detected-gene count is not the same as the retained gene count.
The simulation records its rules in data/synthetic/README.md and simulation-record.txt. simulation-truth.tsv contains generating parameters, not DESeq2 estimates. simulation-samples.tsv records library multipliers, which are not the estimated size factors. plot-examples.tsv prespecifies two gene examples; it is used only for plotting and does not change the fitted model. The seed and rules were fixed before fitting; no discovery count was targeted.
Record: gene count, sample count, group sizes, and the first gene count for A01 and B01.
Next: Check the inputs

title: Check the inputs
text:
From the main project folder, run:
Rscript scripts/R/run_workflow.R data/synthetic results/synthetic --check-only
Expect Input checks passed: 12 samples; 2000 genes; design ~donor + group. The metadata must identify six donors, each with exactly one A and one B sample. The fitted design is ~ donor + group, with A as the reference.
--check-only stops before DESeq2 fitting and does not refresh previous figures or tables.
The script checks required headers, missing and duplicate identifiers, identical sample sets, finite nonnegative integer counts, A and B groups and replication. It aligns metadata rows to the count columns before modelling. It does not prove that the study is well designed.







If the check fails
Look for




Missing file
Current folder or exact filename


Sample IDs differ
Spelling, extra columns, missing rows, case


Counts not integers
Normalized values, decimal entries, text, missing values


Missing replication
Too few independent samples in either group



A first header should be gene_id and sample_id, respectively. Renaming a header cannot fix a transposed count matrix. Do not invent replicates or overwrite raw data just to pass the check.
Checkpoint: explain why passing the file check is necessary but does not establish a valid biological comparison.
Next: Run the analysis

title: Run the analysis
text:
Understand the analysis
From the main project folder, run:
This repeats the input checks, fits DESeq2 and reproduces the figures you previewed. Keep bundled inputs unchanged for the first run. Rerunning replaces the named outputs; resolve any error before interpreting a partially refreshed folder.

title: Run the analysis
text:
Step
What the script does
What to check




Sample summaries
Sums supplied raw counts and counts nonzero genes
These are not overall FASTQ or alignment quality metrics


Filtering
Keeps genes with counts ≥10 in at least two samples
Filtered and original gene counts can differ


Model
Fits ~ donor + group
Contrast is B versus A, accounting for donor; positive effects indicate the first condition


Inference
Estimates size factors, dispersions and condition effects; adjusts p-values
Inspect lfcSE, pvalue, padj and unavailable values


Exploration
Variance-stabilizes retained counts for PCA and distances
These values are not used as differential testing inputs; donor effects remain


Gene display
Plots the post-analysis selected gene alongside two prespecified examples
The first gene is selected after fitting; the other examples are fixed before analysis. Neither display independently confirms p-values

text:
Find the six figures
All filenames below are inside results/synthetic/figures/.







File
Inspect




library-sizes.png
Raw count totals for every sample


sample-pca.png
Condition colours, donor shapes, pair connections and axis percentages

Distances between transformed sample profiles

Average expression versus unshrunken log2 fold change

Unshrunken log2 fold change versus -log10(adjusted p-value)

MA and volcano plots use the original, unshrunken log2 fold-change estimates. Inspect their uncertainty in lfcSE. The volcano omits missing adjusted p-values and floors zero values only for plotting. Colour uses padj < 0.05 without an effect-size cutoff.

Find the supporting numbers
All TSVs below are inside results/synthetic/tables/.







File
Contents

Raw total and detected-gene count for each sample

Model estimates, standard errors, p-values and adjusted p-values

Retained raw counts divided by DESeq2 size factors

Size factor used for each sample

Variance-stabilized retained counts

Sample coordinates and percentages explained

Numerical distances behind the heatmap

Gene ID and normalized values for the post-analysis selected gene

Values and example labels for all three expression panels

Hashes identifying the exact inputs and workflow script



run-log.txt records the design, contrast, filtering, selected gene and software versions. session-info.txt records the R session. Compare these records before investigating differences from bundled previews; software versions may affect final numerical values.
Checkpoint: open all six figures, locate the selected gene in the DE table and confirm the contrast in the run log. Return to the preview page and explain what each figure shows using your own generated outputs.
Next: Verify and explain

title: Verify and explain
text:
1. Check A01 with the supplied script
Verification traces a saved number to its input. Start with A01, then use the gene table and PCA to support a carefully worded observation.
For this bundled version, A01 has 629,417 counts and 1,935 detected genes. Compare these with the input and results/synthetic/tables/sample-qc.tsv. If your input differs, use its actual values and document the version.

title: Verify and explain
text: Rscript scripts/R/verify_sample.R data/synthetic results/synthetic A01

title: Verify and explain
text:
2. Calculate independently
Paste the following into an R console from the main project folder:
x <- read.delim("data/synthetic/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
saved <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/sample-qc.tsv")
manual_total <- sum(x$A01)
manual_detected <- sum(x$A01 > 0)
row <- saved[saved$sample_id == "A01", ]
cat("Total: manual", manual_total, "saved", row$total_counts,
    "agrees", identical(as.numeric(manual_total), as.numeric(row$total_counts)), "\n")
cat("Detected: manual", manual_detected, "saved", row$detected_genes,
    "agrees", identical(as.numeric(manual_detected), as.numeric(row$detected_genes)), "\n")
Both agreement checks should be TRUE. If not, confirm the sample ID, file version and whether the output is from the latest run. Do not edit a saved number to force agreement. This check verifies the count summary, not the DESeq2 fit.

title: Verify and explain
section: 3. Connect a gene result to the question
text:
3. Connect a gene result to the question
result <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/differential-expression.tsv")
print(head(result[, c("gene_id", "log2FoldChange", "pvalue", "padj")]))
cat("Genes with padj < 0.05:", sum(result$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Missing adjusted p-values:", sum(is.na(result$padj)), "\n")
Select one row. Check its sign against group B A in run-log.txt. Compare counts in all A and B replicates; explain why any one raw count cannot reproduce the model’s fold change or p-value. Do not call a gene important merely because its adjusted p-value is small.

title: Verify and explain
text:
4. Explain the PCA with evidence
Open results/synthetic/figures/sample-pca.png. Describe a visible pattern, the percentages on the axes and any overlap. Link your sentence to the figure and at least one number from a table. A PCA cannot establish which genes are differentially expressed. Because all data here are fictional, do not assign a biological cause.
Ready to report: state A01’s independently checked values, one selected gene’s direction and adjusted p-value, and one limitation.

title: Verify and explain
text:
Check the selected-gene figure numerically
In an R console, trace normalized counts back to the raw counts and saved size factors:
raw <- read.delim("data/synthetic/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
size <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/size-factors.tsv")
gene <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/selected-gene-counts.tsv")
v <- as.numeric(unlist(raw[match(gene$gene_id[1], raw$gene_id), gene$sample_id], use.names = FALSE))
sf <- size$size_factor[match(gene$sample_id, size$sample_id)]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(v / sf, gene$normalized_count, tolerance = 1e-8)))
print(gene)
This verifies the arithmetic behind the plotted normalized counts, not the model’s p-values. Check the selected gene in differential-expression.tsv and confirm its direction, standard error and adjusted p-value. Paired normalized-count lines can differ from the overall model estimate because the model combines samples and uncertainty.

title: Verify and explain
text:
Explain all six figures
Write one evidence-based sentence per figure. Quote a sample total, PCA axis percentage, sample-pair distance, gene effect or adjusted p-value from its supporting table. Note unavailable values and avoid treating visually separated samples as a significance test. For airway, distinguish treatment effects from cell-line variation; for synthetic data, keep all biological claims fictional.

title: Verify and explain
text:
Check the two prespecified examples
The extra panels use Gene_0002 and Gene_0003, chosen in the simulation before DESeq2 was fitted. Inspect their observed counts and model estimates:
examples <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/example-gene-counts.tsv")
truth <- read.delim("data/synthetic/simulation-truth.tsv")
result <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/differential-expression.tsv")
ids <- c("Gene_0002", "Gene_0003")
print(examples[examples$gene_id %in% ids, ])
print(truth[truth$gene_id %in% ids, c("gene_id", "simulated_log2_effect")])
print(result[result$gene_id %in% ids, c("gene_id", "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", "padj")])
A zero generating effect does not force identical observed counts or an estimated fold change of exactly zero. Variable donor responses can differ in direction. Each panel uses its own vertical scale; compare numerical values rather than line steepness across panels. Do not remove an example because its p-value does not match an expectation.
Next: Write the report

title: Write the report
text:
Open reports/synthetic-report.qmd. Create it if missing. Paste the template below and replace every bracketed prompt with your checked values. Figure paths are relative to the report in reports/.
---
title: "Synthetic RNA-seq practice report"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
---

## Question and inputs

Which fictional genes differ between group B and group A?

The input consists of 2,000 invented gene rows and 12 fictional samples,
six per group, with the same six donors measured in both conditions. [Confirm these counts from your files.]

## Methods

I checked the count matrix and metadata, then fitted the supplied DESeq2
model `~ donor + group` with B versus A as the contrast. Genes were kept when they
had at least 10 counts in at least two samples. [Add R and DESeq2 versions
from results/synthetic/run-log.txt and the number of genes tested.]

## Verification

For A01, the count total was [number] and [number] genes had nonzero counts.
I recalculated both from gene-counts.tsv and [state agreement with sample-qc.tsv].

## Results

![Library sizes.](../results/synthetic/figures/library-sizes.png)

[Describe the library sizes using checked numbers and state a limitation.]

![PCA.](../results/synthetic/figures/sample-pca.png)

[Describe the pca using checked numbers and state a limitation.]

![Sample-distance heatmap.](../results/synthetic/figures/sample-distances.png)

[Describe the sample-distance heatmap using checked numbers and state a limitation.]

![MA plot.](../results/synthetic/figures/ma-plot.png)

[Describe the ma plot using checked numbers and state a limitation.]

![Volcano plot.](../results/synthetic/figures/volcano.png)

[Describe the volcano plot using checked numbers and state a limitation.]

![Selected-gene expression.](../results/synthetic/figures/selected-gene.png)

[Compare the selected gene, the prespecified null-effect gene and the variable-response gene. Quote checked model estimates and normalized counts. Distinguish generating parameters from fitted estimates; note that panel scales differ.]


## Interpretation and limits

These data are fictional. The plot is exploratory; the gene table reflects
its chosen model and contrast. No claim about a real biological process or
clinical treatment follows from these results.

## Reproducibility

Inputs: data/synthetic/.
Outputs: results/synthetic/.
[Record your run date, exact command and source version.]
Render from the main project folder:
quarto render reports/synthetic-report.qmd --to html
Open the HTML, check the figure displays and remove unfinished bracketed prompts. Rendering the report uses existing outputs and does not rerun DESeq2.
Final check: every number should trace to an input, output table or run record. Next, repeat the seven steps with the airway case study, where cell line is part of the design.

title: Airway example: apply the workflow
text:
The question
Example: dexamethasone experiment. Contrast: treated versus untreated, accounting for cell line.
Run Rscript scripts/R/prepare_airway.R first to export the package counts and metadata.
The input is a matrix of raw integer gene counts and a sample metadata table. Each column represents one biological sample; each row represents one gene. This is a gene-level analysis, starting after sequencing and count generation.

MA plot for the real airway experiment.


Each point is a retained gene with a finite fold-change estimate. The horizontal axis is the mean normalized count on a log scale; the vertical axis is the unshrunken log2 fold change. Colours distinguish adjusted p-values below 0.05, other available values and unavailable values. Low-count estimates may be unstable.

title: See the result
text:
Volcano plot



Volcano plot for the real airway experiment.


Each point has a finite fold-change estimate and an available adjusted p-value. The vertical axis is -log10(adjusted p-value), so higher points have smaller adjusted p-values. The dashed horizontal line marks 0.05. Missing adjusted p-values are omitted; numerical zeros are floored for display. The plot uses unshrunken effects and does not impose an effect-size cutoff.

title: See the result
text:
Selected-gene expression



Selected-gene expression for the real airway experiment.


Each point is a DESeq2 normalized count; lines connect the same donor or cell line across conditions. The title names the gene with the lowest available adjusted p-value (ties follow the saved result order); if none is available, the highest mean normalized count is used. Selection happens after analysis and is illustrative. Normalized counts adjust for size factors; they do not remove donor effects or independently validate the model.

title: Verify and explain
text:
Check the selected-gene figure numerically
In an R console, trace normalized counts back to the raw counts and saved size factors:
raw <- read.delim("data/airway/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
size <- read.delim("results/airway/tables/size-factors.tsv")
gene <- read.delim("results/airway/tables/selected-gene-counts.tsv")
v <- as.numeric(unlist(raw[match(gene$gene_id[1], raw$gene_id), gene$sample_id], use.names = FALSE))
sf <- size$size_factor[match(gene$sample_id, size$sample_id)]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(v / sf, gene$normalized_count, tolerance = 1e-8)))
print(gene)
This verifies the arithmetic behind the plotted normalized counts, not the model’s p-values. Check the selected gene in differential-expression.tsv and confirm its direction, standard error and adjusted p-value. Paired normalized-count lines can differ from the overall model estimate because the model combines samples and uncertainty.

text:
Command
The workflow checks inputs again, saves sample totals, keeps genes with at least 10 counts in at least two samples, fits a DESeq2 negative binomial model, writes the result table, and creates a PCA plot from variance-stabilized values. A positive log2 fold change refers to higher model-estimated expression in the numerator you explicitly set.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text: Key terms

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Raw gene count: reads or fragments assigned to a gene in one sample; do not substitute TPM/FPKM for the count input here.
Library total: sum of raw counts in one column of the supplied count matrix; this is a count-table check, not a sequencing quality metric.
Log2 fold change: estimated treatment/group difference on a base-2 scale for the chosen contrast; positive means higher in the named numerator.
Adjusted p-value: p-value adjusted across many tested genes. NA values need investigation and should not be counted as significant.
Cell line term: in airway, accounts for baseline differences across the four measured cell lines.

text:
Figure methods
The plotting and transformation choices follow the DESeq2 documentation, including sample distances, PCA, MA plots and normalized counts. This guide’s volcano uses adjusted p-values and unshrunken effects. Normalization and transformation do not remove donor effects; donor is handled by the differential expression design.
